# AI Build Kit

> An installable set of commands for an AI coding agent that gives a non-developer a repeatable way to plan, build, check, ship and maintain their own software. It is thirteen skills in the open Agent Skills format: nine commands you type, and four that run in the background. Free, MIT licensed, and it runs inside your own project folder on your own computer.

Who it is for: someone who directs the work and does not read code. The kit is
strongest for internal tools, held by your own team, holding your own data,
with nobody outside relying on them.

Works with: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini CLI, or any coding agent that
can read and edit project files, run shell commands, and use Git.

Install (any supported agent): `npx skills add gwpicard/ai-build-kit`
Install (Claude Code only): `claude plugin marketplace add gwpicard/ai-build-kit`
then `claude plugin install ai-build-kit@ai-build-kit --scope local`
First command to type: `/setup-ai-build-kit`

The nine commands: `/setup-ai-build-kit` founds the project, `/shape` shapes an
idea into a ready piece, `/implement` builds one ready piece, `/queue` shows
everything ready to build, `/fix` repairs a fault cause-first, `/ship` takes the
tool live, `/sync` catches the documents up, `/maintain` is the monthly service
visit, `/what-now` says where the project stands.

How it differs from the alternatives: all-in-one builders such as Lovable, Bolt
and Replit host the app and own the shape of the project. Developer skill packs
such as GitHub Spec Kit, Superpowers and agent-skills carry a similar discipline
but are written for people who read code. AI Build Kit carries that discipline
for people who do not, and opens with a fit check that says when a project needs
a professional developer instead of the kit, or alongside it.

What it does not promise: no warranty, the risk notices will miss things, and it
is not a substitute for a professional developer nor legal, medical, financial
or security advice.
